sanskrit_verse:
प्रतिवेश्यानुवेश्यौ च तस्य मित्रारिबान्धवाः ।
प्रष्टव्याः राजपुरुषैः सामादिभिः उपक्रमैः ॥
transliteration: prativeśyānuveśyau ca tasya mitrāribāndhavāḥ | praṣṭavyāḥ rājapuruṣaiḥ sāmādibhiḥ upakramaiḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The friends, enemies, and relatives of the accused must be examined by royal officers through the application of sāma and other dharmic methods of inquiry.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from the sovereign duty to restore order
Causation arises through relational dynamics, not isolated acts
Capacity-based responsibility extends to all who influence or are influenced by the actor
Restoration logic requires engagement with all relational vectors of the case
Consciousness alignment necessitates comprehensive contextual inquiry
executable_legal_axioms: IF an accused has known relational affiliations THEN those relations MUST be contacted via lawful inquiry protocols
IF a relation is accessible THEN they SHALL undergo examination under sāma-adveṣa-nigraha-vibhāga methodology
IF inquiry reveals misalignment THEN initiate restorative completion process with responsible parties
IF capacity for truth-disclosure exists THEN apply appropriate sāma-based technique for conscious realignment
IF no punitive framing is triggered THEN proceed solely through consciousness-restoration pathways
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this axiom mandates that all judicial inquiries extend beyond individual actors to encompass their relational ecosystems. The court must ensure that state agents utilize sāma and allied dharmic methodologies exclusively, preserving the integrity of consciousness-based justice while maintaining jurisdictional authority over relational networks influencing legal disputes.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality recognizes that actions arise within relational fields; hence, Nyaya demands investigation of these fields without punitive intent. Anupūrvaśaḥ confirms that misalignment manifests sequentially across relationships, requiring proportional response through sāma rather than coercion. Responsibility is assigned based on capacity to restore dharma, not inflict punishment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate sāma-based dialogue with identified relations to reveal underlying causes
Deploy adveṣa techniques to neutralize hostility and align consciousness toward truth
Apply nigraha only where necessary to prevent further disruption of dharmic order
Engage vibhāga strategy to separate false alignments and restore clarity of perception
Complete relational circuit by verifying alignment restoration among all involved parties
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law: Justice flows from consciousness alignment, not punitive force. Relations are integral to dharma's restoration. Inquiry proceeds through sāma alone. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness is the Supreme Adjudicator.
